title: I took my Android phone off silent mode and started using AI ringtones — and I love it
summary: Some imagination and an AI tool is all you need.
body: As someone who grew up in the 90s, I can tell you that ringtones were once a major status symbol. It meant you had a cutting-edge phone capable of such witchcraft, after all. Unfortunately, it took less than a decade for custom ringtones to go from impressive to something most people considered tacky. The rise of smartphones and the bombardment of notifications didn’t help custom ringtones any, either. Even if not as popular as they once were, ringtones are still a great way to add a little flair to your phone, as long as you don’t go overboard. These days, there are tons of sources for ringtones, from dedicated apps to websites that allow you to download ringtone files. Many phones can even take full tunes you own and automatically cut them into ringtones.

We already have AI assistants that can take instructions and execute a series of tasks (not just one at a time) without your supervision — it’s almost like having a human assistant. Google’s Gemini Spark is one such product. In fact, it’s one of the first of its kind to be so easily and widely accessible to end users rather than enterprises. It’s so intuitive that I instinctively gravitate towards Spark whenever I need something done within the Google ecosystem. title: ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude quietly get worse over time. This hidden setting fixes them
summary: Your favorite AI chatbot might be remembering a little too much.
body: I’ve been using LLM-based AI in some capacity for roughly half a decade, and in that time, the industry has changed significantly. Not only have newer competitors like Gemini and Claude arrived on the scene, but older tools like ChatGPT have also evolved dramatically. We’ve seen better third-party app integration, increased reasoning capabilities, and countless other advancements. However, I would argue that the ability to retain memories matters most. Retaining context from previous conversations helps the AI better anticipate your needs within a single session. It also allows the tool to learn more about you, ensuring that future conversations are tailored to your preferences. However, there is a real downside to memory accumulation that not everyone considers. I’ve found that starting with a new AI usually requires significant input to generate the responses I need and fully understand my user profile. Once it reaches this data “sweet spot,” the AI becomes much more pleasant to use. Yet, slowly over time, the experience often seems to degrade again.

But Google has since turned it into a broader AI creative studio, bringing image generation and editing into the same workspace. Gemini Omni then pushed Flow further by letting users combine text, images, audio, and video to create and edit footage. body: Credit: Paul Jones / Android Authority The Samsung Galaxy S5 still has a special place in my heart, purely because I could pop the back off and swap in a fresh battery myself. Phones have come a long way since then, and that kind of easy repairability largely disappeared along the way. But Fairphone has spent years trying to keep the idea alive, and its latest phone brings that philosophy to the US more directly than ever. The Fairphone Gen 6 Plus is the first model the company is selling directly in the US — rather than through Murena — and it runs the standard Google-equipped version of Android. It costs $649 and lets you replace up to 12 components with a single screwdriver, including the battery, display, cameras, and USB-C port. The upgrades over the regular Gen 6 are fairly modest, but we still wanted to know what you made of the package. We asked our readers whether the Gen 6 Plus was hot in a recent poll, and the results could hardly have been more definitive. Take a look for yourself.

AI has earned an overwhelmingly negative perception over the last couple of years. At this point, is there any way for the technology to shed that stigma and become more approachable to the general public? One of the best attempts at that may be Hugging Face’s new tiny duck-like robot. Hugging Face has unveiled a cute bipedal robot known as Microduck. The robot is about 10 inches tall and features 15 motors, a camera, a depth sensor, two inertial measurement units (IMU), and an articulated beak that can pick up objects. According to the company, the duck character was born as a result of the robot’s proportions, beak, and waddling gait.

title: Google is turning AI Mode into an all-in-one travel agent

body: TL;DR Google AI Mode can now track flight prices and email you when fares change, with the feature available in more than 180 countries. AI Mode can show flight and hotel prices in points or miles, making it easier to see whether your travel rewards are worth using. Google is also adding hotel booking directly through AI Mode in the US, letting you choose a room and pay with Google Pay through supported partners. We recently reported that Google made AI Mode in Search much more useful for trip planning. You could connect supported third-party apps, compare live flight and hotel information, look for recommendations, and even build an itinerary without constantly bouncing between different searches. Now, the company is taking that a step further. AI Mode can keep an eye on flight prices for you, show what flights and hotels will cost in points or miles, and even help you book a hotel once you’ve found the right one. So, it’s moving beyond helping you plan a trip and getting much closer to helping you actually book it. The addition I suspect most people will appreciate is flight price tracking. Google Flights has offered price alerts for years, but Google is bringing the feature dir…

title: Google and Pokémon team up for a new special edition Fitbit Air
summary: Gotta catch 'em zzz's.
body: Credit: Google TL;DR Google is launching a new special edition Fitbit Air in collaboration with Pokémon Sleep. The screenless fitness band comes in a Sleepy Blue colorway with a silk print label that features a sleeping Pikachu. Pre-orders start today online and in-store at the Google Store and Target. When the Google Fitbit Air launched, it came in two options: the standard model and the Stephen Curry special edition. Google has now expanded the line to three options by adding a new special edition band. In what feels like a no-brainer collaboration, Google is launching the Fitbit Air Special Edition Pokémon Sleep. If you’re unfamiliar with Pokémon Sleep, it’s a gamified sleep tracking app where players can earn rewards for sleeping longer. As the name of this special edition band suggests, the design of this version of the Fitbit Air draws inspiration from said app. The strap comes in what Google calls a Sleepy Blue colorway, and it includes a silk print label that features a sleeping Pikachu and the Pokémon Sleep logo.

title: Google Tasks could soon pick up this basic feature it should’ve always had
summary: The wait for a dedicated search bar may soon be over.
body: TL;DR We’ve uncovered evidence in the latest version of the Google Tasks app suggesting that a dedicated search bar is finally in the works. We also spotted an early look at the search icon, though the feature is not yet available. This would be a major addition to the Tasks app, given that some of its rival to-do apps already offer a fully functioning search feature. title: Plaud’s new earbuds take notes, then take action
summary: But it’s an AI product first, and earbuds second.
body: TL;DR Plaud is taking its AI note-taking expertise into earbuds with the $249.99 Plaud One Explorer Edition, which can capture and summarize conversations without needing a phone. The bigger pitch is AI that remembers and acts on conversations, using persistent context and Plaud Agent to help with tasks across Gmail, Google Calendar, Notion and Slack. The earbuds are available to pre-order now and ship in late September, with no required subscription and $200 in Plaud credits included. Plaud, the AI startup behind note-taking devices like the Note and NotePin , is taking its ambitions beyond simple recording hardware. Just ahead of IFA getting started next week, the company is already showing off its latest expansion: earbuds. Plaud just announced a pair of AI earbuds called the Plaud One Explorer Edition, and it’s designed for users who want more from a note-taking device than basic recording and summarization.

title: Galaxy S26 FE arrives with upgraded chip and camera features from more expensive Galaxies

body: TL;DR The Galaxy S26 FE has launched with nearly the same hardware as last year’s model but a more capable Exynos chip. The biggest upgrades involve new camera features, such as Horizon Lock and My FanCam, borrowed from more expensive devices. The phone also comes with One UI 9 preinstalled and will get seven years of updates. The Galaxy S25 FE was one of the most fascinating Samsung devices to launch last year. It wasn’t a true flagship, and it didn’t have the best screen, cameras, or chipset; a comparison with the more capable Galaxy S25 — or the newer Galaxy S26 — series phones would easily dwarf it in a tabular comparison. Yet its allure holds up because of the strong value it offers , especially with its battery and charging advantages over the base S series models. Now, Samsung is announcing a follow-up in the form of the new Galaxy S26 FE, which comes with subtle design changes, a new processor, and a host of software upgrades.

title: Survey says readers wouldn’t dare pay to access AI on their older Pixels
summary: Accessing Pixel 11 features on a Pixel 8 for a fee just isn't an attractive proposition for the majority.
body: You can try to run from it or hide from it, but daily mentions of AI from companies or people in your life are inevitable. If you own a Google Pixel , you’ll certainly be well aware of this. Google is continuously rolling out new AI features that require peppier TPUs and chipsets designed for crunching all that data offline. This leaves older Pixel phones, those that are still well supported through software updates or remain quick on their feet in the hardware sense, out in the cold when it comes to new AI smarts.

title: This 10,000mAh phone costs $500 and is available globally
summary: Forget two days of battery life. How does a three-day battery sound?
body: Credit: Hadlee Simons / Android Authority TL;DR Xiaomi has launched the Redmi Note 17 Pro Max in global markets. The phone stands out thanks to a 10,000mAh battery, although Europeans get a 9,210mAh battery. The Redmi Note 17 Pro Max starts at $499. We’ve seen phones with huge batteries in the last 12 months, culminating in devices with ~10,000mAh batteries. This includes the HONOR Win series, HONOR Power 2, and realme P4 Power. Getting your hands on some of these phones might be a problem due to limited availability, but the Redmi Note 17 Pro Max has now arrived in global markets with a 10,000mAh battery. The Redmi Note 17 Pro Max indeed stands out thanks to its absolutely enormous 10,000mAh silicon-carbon battery (16% silicon content). This means it’s quite possibly the most widely available 10,000mAh phone on the market. In saying so, European users get downgraded to a still-impressive 9,210mAh battery. Either way, the company promises 1,600 charging cycles before the battery reaches 80% capacity. It also says you can expect up to three days of usage.

title: Google Photos could soon let you take a shortcut straight to your favorite media
summary: A hidden update suggests Google Photos may soon let you pin favorite albums and folders.
body: TL;DR Google Photos version 7.90 includes an unreleased feature that could let you pin custom shortcuts to the Collections tab. In testing, long-pressing folders, albums, or people allowed pinning them to a horizontal scrolling bar at the top of the app. A dedicated Edit menu could let you reorder pinned items or browse organized library categories to customize your view. When Google replaced the classic Library view with the updated Collections tab, it promised a cleaner way to organize media. However, the top of the screen has remained largely rigid, with Google automatically and unilaterally deciding which shortcuts to highlight while burying your most-used folders. While Google has been testing a cleaner layout for the Collections tab with collapsible sections, the latest app update reveals an unreleased “Pinned” feature in the works that could potentially let you anchor your favorite albums, faces, and folders to the top of the tab.
